clue.text: Upset some runners? Tell me about it!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: knock over a few runner beans
second meaning: the idiom for revealing a secret

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for knocking over a few athletes and is told, wearily, that they have done the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' suggests athletes, but runner beans are a common British garden vegetable, so upsetting some of them is literally a bean spill.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to disclose a secret, which is exactly what an eager listener demands with 'tell me about it'.

clue.text: Bore one can understand

definitions.meaning: first meaning: drill a hole through something
second meaning: see into or grasp something hard to fathom

explanation.surface: A dull person whose talk is at least easy to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' reads as a tedious person, but it is the verb to drill.
explanation.definitionFit: To drill through something and to grasp a difficult idea are both senses of piercing or getting inside, physically or mentally.

clue.text: Unwilling to see a new hat

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or see

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so the letters of the word beside it come out in fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to look at somebody's new headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reluctant or disinclined to do something is the meaning of this adjective, as in loath to admit it.

clue.text: Large installment of cash found in a trench, it turns out

indicators.note: something that turns out differently has been turned about, so the phrase before it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, all seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A big stash of money is dug up from a ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a financial term for a portion or slice of a larger sum, paid or issued in stages.

clue.text: Exterminate scurrying mice often found in the area

parts.note: to end something is to kill it off

indicators.note: creatures scurrying dart about in disorder, so the letters of the word after it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Pest control advice: kill off the mice that run about, a common local nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic disease or species is regularly present in, and native to, a particular region or population.

clue.text: Daring men at first head off to rally

indicators.note: taking the head off a word removes its opening letter
says the trimmed word is placed at the start, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: taken as written, before its first letter goes
daring is boldness, which is courage

explanation.surface: Brave soldiers lead the charge and go off to gather at a rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daring' reads as an adjective but is the noun meaning boldness.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally someone is to hearten or spur them on, which is a close synonym of the verb in the answer.

clue.text: Woman turned up to make one grumble

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
to moan is to grumble

explanation.surface: A woman arrives just to complain.
explanation.walkthrough: Naomi is a biblical woman's name, Ruth's mother-in-law.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a female given name, so any woman called it fits the general definition.

clue.text: Seaside town where such music is sweet

parts.note: Blackpool is a popular seaside resort in Lancashire, England
rock is a kind of music

explanation.surface: A resort where the music is sweet to the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock is also a hard stick of seaside candy with the resort's name running through it, a souvenir sold at British seaside towns.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a stick of hard candy sold at that resort, so it is an example of a confection.

clue.text: Musical man is doleful up to a point

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting up to something means placed directly above it

parts.note: Les is a man's name, short for Leslie
doleful means sad or wretched
S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A man admits he is somewhat sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up to a point' looks like the phrase meaning partly, but it places a compass point below the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the title of a famous stage show based on Victor Hugo's novel, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Help advance an operative

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it
an and a are the same article
a hand is a worker or operative

explanation.surface: A call for assistance to come forward and aid an agent.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to assist or pitch in, a direct equivalent of the verb help.

clue.text: End of street

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a conclusion or finish
second meaning: a residential road, often a dead end, in British addresses

explanation.surface: The far end of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: In British addresses a close is a short street closed at one end, a cul-de-sac.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the finish of something; another is a short residential road blocked at one end.

clue.text: A hundred chat about fool

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters of the word before it are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A crowd of a hundred people gossips about some idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' looks like a noun but is the verb to trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch someone out is to trick or deceive them, the same as fooling them.

clue.text: No music playing as 2,000 join a political movement

indicators.note: playing means toying with the letters, so they come out in a fresh order
joining means the number is added on to the words before it

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them

explanation.surface: A silent protest as two thousand people sign up to a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Communism is a political ideology and the movement built around common ownership of property.

clue.text: Quiet at being put in place

indicators.note: says the short word is placed inside the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written, then opened up
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent when put in their place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiet' reads as an adjective but is the verb meaning to calm.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate someone is to calm or pacify them, which is to quiet them as a verb.

clue.text: Following excitement, there''s a trace of past brilliance

parts.note: after means following
a glow is a warm flush of excitement

explanation.surface: After a thrill, a little of the former sparkle lingers.
explanation.definitionFit: An afterglow is light lingering in the sky after sunset, and figuratively a pleasant lingering memory of success.

clue.text: Leather animal

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a goat-antelope of European mountains

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like one phrase about animal hide, but each defines the answer separately.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a mountain goat-antelope and also the soft pliable skin originally made from it, used for cleaning windows.

clue.text: Sticking out for ex-student, strive to accommodate university reform

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: accommodating something means taking it in, so one letter goes inside the word
to reform is to form again, so the combined letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A former pupil campaigns to get the college to change, and makes himself conspicuous.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtrusive means noticeably projecting or prominent, so it describes something that sticks out.

clue.text: Surpass in open work

parts.note: overt means done openly
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Excelling in an unconfined job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open work' reads like openwork, a decorative pattern of holes, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtop is to rise above something, and so to exceed or outdo it.

clue.text: Brawl, being high on drink

indicators.note: on means the word before it is attached to the drink word

parts.note: punch is a mixed drink served from a bowl
up means high

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out because someone is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch-up is British slang for a fist fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A punch-up is an informal word for a fist fight, which is what a brawl is.

clue.text: Fine-sounding American and better half feel too hot

indicators.note: sounding says only the spoken form of the word matters, not its spelling

parts.note: swell is slang for fine or excellent

indicators.note: taking half of the word means dropping its first three letters

parts.note: taken as written, before half goes
gives no letters: it tells you the slang sense of fine is an American one

explanation.surface: An American and his spouse are uncomfortably warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better half' looks like a spouse, but it is the second half of the word better.
explanation.definitionFit: To swelter is to be oppressively hot and sweaty in the heat.

clue.text: Pan craft

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cooking vessel for steaming food

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan craft' sounds like a skill with cookware, but each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a perforated cooking pot for steaming vegetables and also a ship driven by steam.

clue.text: Again order back to the stove

parts.note: the rear is the back
a range is a large cooking stove

explanation.surface: Instructions once more to go back to the cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange is to put into a different order, that is, to order things anew.

clue.text: Shade of warning

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the traffic light that signals caution

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it means a hint of caution; split, it is a colour and a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a golden-orange colour and also the middle traffic light that warns drivers the signal is changing.

clue.text: Fathom precisely

definitions.meaning: first meaning: measure the depth of water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fathom precisely' sounds like understanding exactly, but each word is its own meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Sounding water with a weighted line is plumbing it, and the adverb means exactly or squarely.

clue.text: Window No. 50 for the team

parts.note: a pane is a sheet of glass in a window
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A window marked number fifty is reserved for a squad.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a group of people assembled to judge, advise or discuss, as on a quiz show.

clue.text: Accountant (to a degree) and student are in league

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: An accountant and a student are, to some extent, conspiring together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a degree' looks like the phrase meaning somewhat, but it just supplies a university degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabal is a secret faction or alliance of plotters, a sinister kind of league.

clue.text: Hume frames final development of people's existence

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so the philosopher's name goes around the other letters

parts.note: the Scottish philosopher's name taken as written

indicators.note: a development changes the form of something, so the next word's letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: The philosopher David Hume sets out the ultimate stage of humanity's being.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the life of humankind, the existence of persons generally.

clue.text: To trace an analogy, no one wins the match

parts.note: a draw is a result where neither side wins
a parallel is a match or equivalent

explanation.surface: Comparing things, like a game that ends with no winner.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to point out a likeness or comparison between two things.
